days.bt: Types, functions, objects, destructuring, modules, interfaces. Write 10 small exercises without copy-paste.
days.itt: Valid Palindrome, Valid Anagram. Learn the two-pointer pattern.

days.bt: Promises, async/await, fetch, fs, npm scripts. Build a CLI script that calls a public API.
days.itt: Group Anagrams, Longest Consecutive Sequence.

days.bt: Terminal basics (cd, ls, grep, chmod, curl), env vars, SSH basics. Review HTTP methods, status codes, DNS, ports.

days.bt: SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING. Do 20 queries on SQLZoo or HackerRank SQL.

days.bt: Update your notes file with every concept you got stuck on. Plan Week 2.

days.bt: Register/login, bcrypt hashing, JWT, auth middleware, protected routes.
days.itt: Subsets, Generate Parentheses.

days.bt: Zod validation, central error middleware, correct status codes, basic logging.

days.itt: Number of Islands, Clone Graph.

days.bt: Fix any failing tests. Update notes. Plan Week 3.
days.itt: Timed set of 3 problems (1 easy, 2 medium) on HackerRank or LeetCode. Review every solution afterward.

days.bt: Components, props, state, useState/useEffect, lists, conditional rendering. Build a small to-do app.
days.itt: Kth Largest Element in an Array, Top K Frequent Elements.

days.bt: Build main screens for the capstone: list and create. Keep state simple, reuse components.
days.itt: Four pillars, class vs interface vs abstract class, composition vs inheritance. Model a parking lot or library in TypeScript classes. Plus 1 warm-up problem.

days.bt: Edit and delete screens. Make the main feature usable end to end.
days.itt: Explain each SOLID principle with an example. Implement Singleton, Factory, Observer in TypeScript. Refactor one messy function in your project. Plus 1 problem.

days.bt: Responsive layout, empty states, form validation messages, consistent spacing. Test at phone width.
days.itt: Joins, GROUP BY/HAVING, subqueries, window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK), indexes. Solve 10 LeetCode SQL problems.
days.rv: Database Systems; UI/UX Design and Prototyping

days.bt: Demo run-through. List and fix 5 bugs. Update notes. Plan Week 4.
days.itt: Two mediums under time. Talk through your approach out loud and test edge cases.

days.bt: Dockerfile for the API. docker-compose with API + PostgreSQL. Run everything with one command.
days.itt: Scaling, load balancers, caching, CDN, replication (System Design Primer). Sketch a URL shortener. Plus 1 problem.
days.dl: docker compose up works; design sketch

days.bt: Workflow that installs, lints and tests on every push. Add a status badge to the README.
days.itt: Message queues, concurrency, rate limiting, SQL vs NoSQL. Sketch a booking system. Plus 1 problem.

days.bt: Deploy API + database (Render/Railway) and frontend (Vercel). Set environment secrets. Get a public URL.
days.itt: Write your own answers: URL-to-page, REST, JWT vs sessions, CORS, ACID, N+1, process vs thread. Plus 1 problem.

days.bt: Structured logging, health-check endpoint, basic metrics. Note how Prometheus/Grafana would use them.

days.bt: README: what it does, stack, setup, screenshots, architecture diagram, what you would improve.
days.itt: STAR stories: project, conflict, failure, teamwork. Practice 'Tell me about yourself' in 60 seconds. Plus 1 problem.

days.bt: Tailor CV to the Agoda job description. Pin best repos. Update LinkedIn. Link the live demo.

days.bt: Fix rough edges. Be ready to explain every file and design choice.
days.itt: 45-minute mock system design plus a 10-minute project walkthrough. Fix the weak spots.

days.bt: Apply to Agoda and 4+ other big companies (Grab, Shopee, LINE MAN Wongnai, banks' tech arms). Track each in a sheet.
days.itt: Timed set of 3 problems. Review each solution, note topic gaps.

days.bt: Plan the next 30 days: harder project, more system design.
days.itt: Review the Checklist sheet. List your top 3 weak topics. Plan: 2 DSA problems per day and 1 mock per week.

chk.q: Explain encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction with one real example each
Class vs interface vs abstract class: when do you use each?
Composition vs inheritance: which do you prefer and why?
Explain each SOLID principle with a short example
When would you use Singleton, Factory and Observer?
Method overloading vs overriding
Big-O of common operations: array, hash map, sorted array, BST, sorting
When do you pick a hash map, a heap, a stack or a queue?
BFS vs DFS: when to use each, and their complexity
Walk through how you approach an unfamiliar problem (clarify, example, brute force, optimize, test)
What happens when you type a URL into the browser and press Enter?
REST vs GraphQL; what makes an HTTP method idempotent?
JWT vs session cookies: trade-offs and where to store the token
What is CORS and why does it exist?
Authentication vs authorization
Process vs thread; what is a race condition and a deadlock?
SQL vs NoSQL: when do you choose each?
What is an index, and what is the trade-off?
ACID and transaction isolation levels in simple words
What is the N+1 query problem and how do you fix it?
Sketch a URL shortener: API, database, scaling, caching
Load balancer, horizontal vs vertical scaling, caching layers
When would you add a message queue?
How would you monitor your service? (logs, metrics, alerts, Prometheus/Grafana)
Tell me about yourself in 60 seconds
Describe a project you are proud of (STAR format)
A conflict or failure and what you learned
Why Agoda (or this company)? Why this role?
